items: whisk vinegar with salt until the salt dissolves
slowly stream in the oil while whisking
dress the salad just before serving
reveal: Mustard is an emulsifier: it keeps the oil and vinegar suspended instead of separating. Salting the vinegar first seasons the whole dressing evenly.

items: take the roast out of the oven
move it to a board with a juice channel
reveal: Resting lets the muscle fibres relax and reabsorb juices; carving too early loses them to the board. Cutting across the grain shortens the tough fibres.
Complete metamorphosis: the caterpillar's tissues are largely rebuilt inside the pupa. A monarch takes about a month from egg to adult.

items: the moist air rises and cools
spiral bands wrap around the clear eye
landfall cuts off the energy source
reveal: The fuel is warm surface water — that is why hurricanes weaken quickly over land, and why they cannot form within about 5° of the equator, where there is no Coriolis force to spin them up.

rule: The first seventy years of human flight
items: the Wright brothers' first powered flight (1903)
the first jet airliner enters service (1952)
reveal: From a 12-second hop to a scheduled supersonic service in 73 years. Two of those aircraft — the 747 and Concorde — were designed in the same decade and flew for the next half century.

rule: The fall of the Berlin Wall and reunification
items: reform begins in the Soviet Union
Hungary opens its border to the West (1989)
mass protests spread across East Germany
the Wall's crossings are opened (9 November 1989)
reveal: The Wall fell because of a press conference: a spokesman misread a note about relaxed travel rules and said they took effect immediately, and tens of thousands went to the checkpoints that evening.

rule: Ordering the parts of a formal letter
reveal: The block ordering is not arbitrary: the reader learns who is writing, when, and to whom before reading a word of the argument. Everything after the signature — enclosures, postscripts — sits outside the main body.
Save the strongest argument for second-to-last: an audience remembers the middle of a speech least. The close has to be quotable, because that is the line they carry out of the room.

rule: Tying a shoelace with the loop method
items: pass one lace under the other and pull tight
form a loop with each lace
cross the loops over each other
push one loop through the hole
reveal: The 'bunny ears' method works for children, but the same knot has a faster one-loop variant. A knot that comes undone is usually an imbalance knot — the starting cross is backwards.

items: check the expiry date and the lead time
wait for processing, then collect or receive it
reveal: Many countries require the passport to be valid for six months beyond your travel date, so the deadline is earlier than the printed expiry. Photo rejections are the single most common cause of delay.

rule: Units of digital storage, smallest to largest
reveal: Eight bits to a byte. Storage is decimal (1,000) while memory is binary (1,024), which is why a '500 GB' drive shows up as roughly 465 GB in an operating system.

rule: Periods of the Mesozoic Era, earliest to latest
reveal: Triassic, Jurassic, Cretaceous — the three periods that together make up the Mesozoic, ending 66 million years ago with the impact that ended the non-avian dinosaurs.
Complete metamorphosis. Whether the adult emerges as a worker or a queen is decided by diet: royal jelly throughout the larval stage produces a queen.

rule: One heartbeat through the heart's chambers
items: deoxygenated blood enters the right atrium
it flows into the right ventricle
the right ventricle pumps it to the lungs
oxygenated blood returns to the left atrium
it flows into the left ventricle
the left ventricle pumps it out through the aorta
reveal: The left ventricle has a thicker wall than the right because it drives blood through the entire body rather than only to the lungs. Valves between the chambers stop any backflow.
